The Workshare and Revenue Allocation article and/or Exhibit A reflect Meridian at 38% of the $215M estimated TCV.
The Workshare and Revenue Allocation article and/or Exhibit A reflect Meridian's share as $81,700,000.
The workshare/revenue allocation covers the 5-year base period.
The workshare/revenue allocation covers three 1-year option periods.
The agreement states a target fixed-fee rate of 7.5% on estimated costs.

The financial provisions or Exhibit A reference Meridian's estimated fee of approximately $5,700,000.
The Exclusivity and Non-Compete article limits exclusivity to solicitation HC1028-25-R-0042 only.
The agreement provides that exclusivity terminates 12 months after proposal submission if no award is made (i.e., June 20, 2026 or an equivalent description).
The agreement provides that exclusivity terminates 60 days after formal agency cancellation of the solicitation.
The B&P Cost Sharing article and/or Exhibit B state total estimated B&P costs of $1,800,000.
The agreement states Vantage's B&P share as 65%.
The agreement states Vantage's B&P share as $1,170,000.
The agreement states Meridian's B&P share as 35%.
The agreement states Meridian's B&P share as $630,000.
The agreement states that each party's B&P costs are non-refundable regardless of outcome.
The IP article preserves each party's sole ownership of its background/pre-existing IP.
The IP article grants a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to background IP limited to proposal preparation and contract performance.
The IP article assigns foreground IP to the developing party.
The IP article grants the other party a cross-license to foreground IP solely for Government contract performance.
The IP article references DFARS 252.227-7014 (Rights in Other Than Commercial Computer Software and Other Than Commercial Computer Software Documentation) for Government rights.
The IP article references DFARS 252.227-7018 (Rights in Other Than Commercial Technical Data and Computer Software — Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Program) for Government rights.
The OCI Mitigation article and/or Exhibit D disclose Meridian's existing DISA SETI-II Task Order D4017.
The disclosure states the SETI-II Task Order D4017 value of $6,200,000.
The disclosure states the SETI-II Task Order D4017 period of performance runs through December 31, 2025.
The disclosure states Meridian performs advisory cybersecurity assessments for the same DISA program office under SETI-II Task Order D4017.
The agreement requires Meridian to establish a firewall segregating SETI-II advisory personnel from Sentinel Shield teams.
The agreement states Meridian will not seek extension of SETI-II Task Order D4017.
The agreement identifies BridgePoint Consulting Group, LLC as the independent OCI mitigation auditor.
The Insurance Requirements article and/or Exhibit C specify Meridian CGL at $2,000,000 per occurrence.
The Insurance Requirements article and/or Exhibit C specify Meridian CGL at $5,000,000 aggregate.
The agreement specifies Meridian Professional Liability (E&O) at $10,000,000 per claim.
The agreement specifies Meridian Professional Liability (E&O) at $10,000,000 aggregate.
The agreement specifies Meridian Cyber Liability at $5,000,000.
The agreement specifies Vantage CGL at $5,000,000 per occurrence.
The agreement specifies Vantage CGL at $10,000,000 aggregate.
The agreement specifies Vantage Professional Liability (E&O) at $10,000,000.
The agreement specifies Vantage Cyber Liability at $10,000,000.
The Indemnification article caps Meridian's indemnification to Vantage at the lesser of $81,700,000 (Meridian's workshare value) or 1× aggregate subcontract value invoiced to date.
The Indemnification article caps Vantage's indemnification to Meridian at 1× aggregate payments made to Meridian to date.
The agreement carves IP infringement out from the indemnification caps so that it is uncapped.
The agreement carves willful misconduct out from the indemnification caps so that it is uncapped.
The Termination article provides for pre-award termination for convenience by either party if no Government contract has been awarded.
The pre-award termination for convenience requires 30 days' written notice.
The Termination article provides for post-award termination for cause upon material breach.
The post-award termination for cause provides a 30-day cure period.
The Termination article provides that failure to cure permits immediate termination.
The agreement permits either party to terminate if the other party undergoes a greater than 50% ownership transfer without prior written consent.
The Dispute Resolution article requires mandatory senior-executive negotiation as a condition precedent to arbitration.
The senior-executive negotiation period is 30 calendar days.
The agreement specifies binding arbitration under AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules.
The agreement specifies the arbitration venue as Fairfax County, Virginia.
The agreement specifies a panel of 3 arbitrators.
The Governing Law provision specifies the Commonwealth of Virginia.
The Governing Law provision applies Virginia law without regard to conflicts-of-law principles.

The Notices provision lists Meridian's attention line as Attn: Rachel S. Feinberg, Director of Contracts.
